eli5.text: When you accept an advertiser-sponsored task in the Freebuff CLI, the assistant can now no longer run commands that break out of your project to touch the rest of your computer. Specifically, it refuses to launch into Windows Subsystem for Linux, run destructive database commands like drop, reset, or wipe, or control containers and images that might affect your own running services. You don't need to do anything differently, but if an advertiser's procedure tries one of these commands, the assistant stops and reports the refusal instead of carrying it out.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.200 is a security and access update for the free coding-assistant CLI. The main user-facing change is that GPT-6 Luna and MiMo 2.6 Pro are now fully open to every full-access user, no longer restricted only to the US or paid accounts, while still locked behind a plan for limited-tier users. Sponsored runs - tasks paid for by an advertiser - got safer: they can no longer enter the Windows Subsystem for Linux, can no longer drop or reset databases, and can no longer build, start, stop, or remove your containers (for example, docker compose up now stops). Sponsored runs can also now declare and receive a single encrypted credential, like an API key, which gets injected into that run only and is hidden from logs and model output. A small clipboard fix also now warns Linux users when a copy only reached the terminal (not the clipboard) and tells them how to fix it. Tests also switched their default CPM-ad setting off, which only affects automated test runs, not production.

ai.summary: The agent runtime now names media and long base64 payloads instead of serializing their bytes into the compaction request, so a screenshot-heavy thread compacts in one pass instead of restarting across many large summarizer calls. The SDK's truncateRunStateAtUserTurn gains an optional totalUserTurns parameter that, when supplied, places the rewind boundary from the end of messageHistory rather than counting user turns from the start, which previously miscounted Stop notes and compaction summaries as user turns. eli5.text: The AI assistant no longer wastes time re-summarizing entire chat histories when those histories contain large screenshots or image files. Previously, every screenshot a tool returned (like a picture of code or a webpage) was crammed into the text the assistant tried to summarize, turning one quick summary into dozens of slow rounds. Now those images are skipped and named instead, so a session full of screenshots compacts in a single step. This speeds up and stabilizes the assistant's memory-trimming for anyone editing earlier parts of a long conversation, since the part that picks where to rewind now counts from the end of the chat instead of getting confused by internal notes and saved summaries.

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 0.0.203 adds binary elision and user-turn-bounded truncation to long conversations. The release introduces two main behaviors: when the assistant condenses a long chat into a shorter summary, large base64 blobs such as screenshots are now named and omitted instead of being copied into the summary request, which avoids very large summarization calls. The second change makes editing or undoing a message in a long thread keep the right number of past user turns by counting only the user prompts the runtime records, and by placing the cut relative to the end of the history when the host reports total user turns. As a result, stopping a run and then editing a message no longer throws away most of the conversation, and image heavy threads summarize without repeatedly streaming huge base64 payloads. These changes apply to users editing or undoing across compacted conversations and to Desktop sessions that carry screenshots in their history. The release evidence is incomplete regarding any other user facing behavior, so no further features or safety gains are described here.

entries.summary: New files: `cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts`.

ai.title: CLI ships previous-launcher fatal crash telemetry on next launch
ai.summary: A new fatal-crash-report module writes a bounded crash report (error name, first 300 chars of message, first 20 stack frames, version/platform/uptime, and whether a Freebuff hour was held) synchronously to last-fatal-crash.json as the process exits, and the next launch reads and ships it as a cli.fatal_crash analytics event before the session begins. The report is dropped if older than 7 days or corrupt, recording and reading never throw, and a report is consumed exactly once. Concurrently, useGravityAd now returns a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton via visibleResponseAds so hidden inline ads no longer re-trigger chat's layout effect each render, and SDK event handlers are wrapped in isolateUiHandler so a throwing UI update is logged and the agent run continues instead of becoming an unhandled fatal rejection. SIGPIPE is now explicitly ignored and excluded from CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS so a broken-pipe write no longer tears down the renderer and risks an exit-141 death, and external exits (terminal closed, killed, launcher gone) keep an active Freebuff hour for resume via the new keepSlotForResume path instead of ending it.
ai.evidence: New module cli/src/utils/fatal-crash-report.ts defines recordFatalCrashSync and takePreviousFatalCrash; cli/src/index.tsx calls takePreviousFatalCrash at launch and fires AnalyticsEvent.CLI_FATAL_CRASH, and common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts adds CLI_FATAL_CRASH='cli.fatal_crash' to the enum; common/src/util/analytics-sampling.ts adds CLI_FATAL_CRASH to ALWAYS_TRACK_EVENTS.

changes.what: Added fatal-crash-report.ts with recordFatalCrashSync writing a bounded report to last-fatal-crash.json and takePreviousFatalCrash reading and consuming it; index.tsx ships the previous report as cli.fatal_crash on launch.

Added CLI_RENDERER_EXIT_SIGNALS (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGQUIT, SIGABRT, SIGHUP, SIGBREAK, SIGBUS, excluding SIGPIPE) and an explicit SIGPIPE ignore handler in renderer-cleanup.ts; createCliRenderer now uses these signals so SIGPIPE no longer destroys the renderer.
External exits (terminal closed, killed, launcher gone) now call keepSlotForResume to retain an active Freebuff hour for the next launch instead of ending it.

Added visibleResponseAds and a frozen NO_RESPONSE_ADS singleton in use-gravity-ad.ts, and chat.tsx now passes visibleResponseAds(showInlineAds, responseAds) into the message-block context so hidden ads keep a stable identity.

Wrapped createStreamChunkHandler and createEventHandler in isolateUiHandler so a throwing SDK event updates are logged (bounded to MAX_UI_HANDLER_FAILURE_LOGS_PER_RUN per run) and the agent run continues instead of fatal-exiting.

eli5.text: When the assistant app crashes, it now saves a small note about the crash locally as it shuts down, and the next time you open the app it reads that note and sends a quiet crash report. This helps fix recurring crashes without asking you for screenshots, and the report is deleted after use. A broken-pipe write (like output redirected to a closed command) no longer kills the app with a confusing exit-code-141, hidden inline ads no longer cause the chat to re-render in a loop, and if the app is closed by an outside signal while a free session is running, that free time is kept for the next launch instead of being ended early. The crash report only ever ships once and is ignored if it is older than a week or unreadable, so it never blocks a normal startup.

eli5.text: This Freebuff CLI release (0.0.204) keeps your coding session safer when things go wrong behind the scenes. When the app crashes or the terminal is closed unexpectedly, your paid-for session time is now preserved so the next time you open the tool, it picks up where it left off instead of charging you again. Crash details are now captured locally and sent along on the next startup for debugging, rather than disappearing when the process exits. The chat interface stops a looping error where hiding ads could cause a React crash that killed your work, and signal handlers (like SIGTERM/SIGHUP) now route through a shared external-exit path that keeps your session alive instead of ending it. Overall, the release reduces the chance that a crash, terminal close, or signal kills both your run and your session credit, and helps the team see what went wrong after the fact.
